feature1.prompt: Meta.ordering fields must not be included in GROUP BY clause. This continues the (closed) ticket. It was not properly fixed in commit [0ddb4ebf]: while ORDER BY is removed when Meta.ordering is used, the GROUP BY clause still incorrectly includes Meta.ordering fields, leading to wrong aggregation.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on modifying the SQL generation logic in the Django ORM. The goal is to adjust the get_group_by method so that when _meta_ordering is not set, the method excludes any fields originating from Meta.ordering from the GROUP BY clause. The implementation must ensure that no extra grouping columns are added, thus avoiding unintended aggregation results.
feature1.entrypoint: Modify the file django/db/models/sql/compiler.py. In the get_group_by method (starting around line 125 in the diff), introduce a condition to check if _meta_ordering is not active before iterating over order_by expressions. This change will ensure that only the correct columns are used in the GROUP BY clause.

feature2.prompt: Meta.ordering fields must not be included in GROUP BY clause. The issue arises because, although the ORDER BY clause is modified when Meta.ordering is used, the GROUP BY clause still incorporates these fields, resulting in incorrect aggregation. This behavior must be validated to ensure that aggregation does not inadvertently include fields specified in Meta.ordering.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves adding a new test case to verify that the GROUP BY clause excludes Meta.ordering fields. The test should set up a scenario where Article objects have their ordering applied by default, then perform an aggregation (using Count or a similar function) and check that the results reflect the correct grouping without interference from ordering fields. The new test method must clearly document the expected aggregation behavior.
feature2.entrypoint: Add a new test method named test_default_ordering_does_not_affect_group_by in the tests/ordering/tests.py file. The test should update Article objects (for example, by changing the author field) and then perform a values-and-annotate query to verify that the GROUP BY clause correctly groups records without including any fields from Meta.ordering.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the Django ORM aggregation and ordering logic. In particular, the get_group_by method in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py and the ordering test file tests/ordering/tests.py are shared resources.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 must implement the fix so that Meta.ordering fields are excluded from the GROUP BY clause. Feature2 will add a test case that validates this behavior. Once both are complete, integration testing should be performed to ensure that the new SQL generation logic works as expected and that the test case passes without regressions.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on feature1 and feature2 must coordinate closely. The implementer of feature1 should communicate the details of the SQL generation fix so that the test added in feature2 accurately captures the intended behavior. Regular code reviews and integration meetings are recommended to resolve any discrepancies.
